meta.title: Polish Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 802 expressions · 15 everyday, 711 idioms, 76 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 802 Polish set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 15 everyday phrases, 711 idioms and 76 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Polish → English (see the Polish, recall the meaning) and English → Polish (see an English meaning, recall the Polish) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the level decks, Polish A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of them, so they can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases or interjections and does not mark as idiomatic — the formulas a speaker uses as one piece (jeszcze raz, na pomoc, która godzina, nazywam się …); sentences a learner builds from the level decks' words ("I don't eat meat", "I'm from …") are left out. The IDIOMS are the expressions with a sense Wiktionary marks as idiomatic, of any part of speech — set phrases like nie ma, nie wiem, mieć nadzieję, w stanie as much as images like robić z igły widły, bułka z masłem, czytać między wierszami, trzymać kciuki. The PROVERBS are the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (lepiej późno niż wcale, miłość jest ślepa, cel uświęca środki …). WHICH ONES, since there are far more than a deck: Wiktionary has 3,366 such Polish expressions that no level teaches, and this deck takes the 802 of them that occur in at least one of Tatoeba's Polish sentences with an English translation — an expression that begins with a verb being found with that verb in any form. That is a test of being in use, not an official list. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of those sentences contain them. Real example sentences come with 802 of the 802, three apiece for 236, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Meanings and parts of speech: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences and the count that chooses and orders the expressions: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
